title.zh: 卷一百〇八 載記第八 慕容廆
title.raw: 卷一百〇八 載記第八 慕容廆 Volume 108 Records 8: Murong Hui

sentences.zh: 慕容廆

translations.literal: Murong Hui
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui

sentences.zh: 慕容廆，字弈洛瑰，昌黎棘城鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Murong Hui, courtesy name Yiluogui, was a Xianbei of Jicheng in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: A Xianbei leader from Jicheng in Changli, style Yiluogui.

sentences.zh: 其先有熊氏之苗裔，世居北夷，邑于紫蒙之野，號曰東胡。

translations.literal: His ancestors were descendants of the Youxiong clan; for generations they dwelt among the northern tribes, built their seat in the wilds of Zimeng, and were called Eastern Hu.
translations.idiomatic: They claimed Youxiong ancestry, lived beyond the frontier at Zimeng, and were known as Eastern Hu.

sentences.zh: 其後與匈奴並盛，控弦之士二十餘萬，風俗官號與匈奴略同。

translations.literal: Later they rose alongside the Xiongnu with more than two hundred thousand bowmen; customs and titles broadly matched the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: They matched the Xiongnu in strength—two hundred thousand horsemen with parallel customs.

sentences.zh: 秦漢之際為匈奴所敗，分保鮮卑山，因以為號。

translations.literal: At the Qin-Han transition the Xiongnu defeated them; they split off to hold Mount Xianbei and took that name.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han defeat drove them onto Xianbei Mountain and gave them their tribal name.

sentences.zh: 曾祖莫護跋，魏初率其諸部入居遼西，從宣帝伐公孫氏有功，拜率義王，始建國於棘城之北。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Mohuba in early Wei led his tribes into western Liaoxi, followed Emperor Xuan on campaign against the Gongsun clan, earned merit, was enfeoffed Prince of Shuaiyi, and first founded a state north of Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mohuba earned Wei's trust against the Gongsuns and planted Murong power north of Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 時燕代多冠步搖冠，莫護跋見而好之，乃斂發襲冠，諸部因呼之為步搖，其後音訛，遂為慕容焉。

translations.literal: In Yan and Dai many wore buyao crowns; Mohuba admired them, tucked his hair under such a crown, and the tribes called him Buyao—later slip of the tongue turned the name into Murong.
translations.idiomatic: A hat nicknamed him Buyao until listeners corrupted it into Murong.

sentences.zh: 或云慕二儀之德，繼三光之容，遂以慕容為氏。

translations.literal: Another tale says they revered the virtue of the Two Principles and the radiance of the Three Lights, hence the surname Murong.
translations.idiomatic: Another etymology ties Murong to reverence for Heaven, Earth, and the luminaries.

sentences.zh: 祖木延，左賢王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Muyan held the title Left Wise Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Muyan served as Left Wise Prince.

sentences.zh: 父涉歸，以全柳城之功，進拜鮮卑單于，遷邑於遼東北，於是漸慕諸夏之風矣。

translations.literal: His father Shegui, for preserving Liucheng intact, was promoted Xianbei Shanyu and moved the seat northeast into Liaodong; there they gradually admired Central Plains refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Shegui won the Shanyu title for Liucheng and guided the clan toward Chinese ways.

sentences.zh: 廆幼而魁岸，美姿貌，身長八尺，雄傑有大度。

translations.literal: From youth Hui was imposing and handsome, eight chi tall, heroic and magnanimous.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he stood eight chi tall—striking, heroic, broad.

sentences.zh: 安北將軍張華雅有知人之鑒，廆童丱時往謁之，華甚歎異，謂曰：「君至長必為命世之器，匡難濟時者也。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Zhang Hua was famed for judging men; while still a boy Hui visited him. Hua marveled and said, "When grown you will be an instrument for the age—one who rectifies disaster and aids the times."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua predicted the boy would master an age of turmoil.

sentences.zh: 」因以所服簪幘遺廆，結殷勤而別。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gave Hui his own hairpin and turban as gifts and parted with earnest warmth.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Hui his cap pin and turban as farewell gifts.

sentences.zh: 涉歸死，其弟耐篡位，將謀殺廆，廆亡潛以避禍。

translations.literal: When Shegui died, his younger brother Nai seized the throne and plotted to murder Hui; Hui fled into hiding to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Nai seized power and hunted him until kinsmen restored Hui.

sentences.zh: 後國人殺耐，迎廆立之。

translations.literal: Later the tribes killed Nai and welcomed Hui to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The tribe slew Nai and enthroned Hui.

sentences.zh: 初，涉歸有憾于宇文鮮卑，廆將修先君之怨，表請討之。

translations.literal: At first Shegui had quarreled with the Yuwen Xianbei; Hui meant to settle his father's score and memorialized for permission to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He sought imperial blessing to avenge Shegui's feud with the Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 武帝弗許。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: The western Jin court refused.

sentences.zh: 廆怒，入寇遼西，殺略甚眾。

translations.literal: Angered, Hui raided western Liaoxi and slaughtered widely.
translations.idiomatic: He lashed out with raids across western Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 帝遣幽州諸軍討廆，戰於肥如，廆眾大敗。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Youzhou forces against him; they fought at Feiru and Hui's army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops routed him at Feiru.

sentences.zh: 自後復掠昌黎，每歲不絕。

translations.literal: Afterward he again pillaged Changli year after year without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He kept harassing Changli afterward.

sentences.zh: 又率眾東伐扶余，扶余王依慮自殺，廆夷其國城，驅萬餘人而歸。

translations.literal: He also led hosts east against Buyeo; King Yilü of Buyeo killed himself; Hui leveled the capital, drove off ten thousand captives, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered Buyeo, drove its king to suicide, and dragged captives home.

sentences.zh: 東夷校尉何龕遣督護賈沈將迎立依慮之子為王，廆遣其將孫丁率騎邀之。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Eastern Yi He Kan sent protector Jia Shen to install Yilü's son as king; Hui sent general Sun Ding with cavalry to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: He Kan tried to crown a new Buyeo king while Murong ambushed the escort.

sentences.zh: 沈力戰斬丁，遂復扶余之國。

translations.literal: Shen fought hard, beheaded Ding, and restored Buyeo's kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Shen killed Sun Ding and restored Buyeo.

sentences.zh: 廆謀於其眾曰：「吾先公以來世奉中國，且華裔理殊，強弱固別，豈能與晉競乎？

translations.literal: Hui consulted his followers: "Since our forefathers we have honored China; Chinese and barbarian orders differ and strength is uneven—how can we vie with Jin?
translations.idiomatic: He urged submission to Jin—barbarians could not long defy the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 何為不和以害吾百姓邪！

translations.literal: Why not make peace rather than harm our people!"
translations.idiomatic: He chose peace over wasting herdsmen.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使來降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys west to surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，拜為鮮卑都督。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and appointed him Xianbei Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him commander over the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 廆致敬於東夷府，巾衣詣門，抗士大夫之禮。

translations.literal: Hui paid respects at the Eastern Yi headquarters, wearing civilian cap and robe at the gate like a scholar-official.
translations.idiomatic: He appeared at He Kan's yamen in scholar dress.

sentences.zh: 何龕嚴兵引見，廆乃改服戎衣而入。

translations.literal: Kan arrayed troops for the audience; Hui changed into armor before entering.
translations.idiomatic: When Kan lined up troops, Hui donned armor instead.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，廆曰：「主人不以禮，賓復何為哉！

translations.literal: Asked why, Hui said, "If the host shows no courtesy, what should a guest do!"
translations.idiomatic: He insisted hosts owe ritual before guests.

sentences.zh: 」龕聞而慚之，彌加敬憚。

translations.literal: Kan, ashamed, treated him with deeper awe.
translations.idiomatic: Kan swallowed his pride and deferred.

sentences.zh: 時東胡宇文鮮卑段部以廆威德日廣，懼有吞併之計，因為寇掠，往來不絕。

translations.literal: Then the Yuwen and Duan branches of Eastern Hu Xianbei, fearing Hui's spreading might meant annexation, raided ceaselessly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen and Duan rivals feared annexation and raided endlessly.

sentences.zh: 廆卑辭厚幣以撫之。

translations.literal: Hui answered them with humble words and lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He bought quiet with gifts and soft words.

sentences.zh: 太康十年，廆又遷於徒河之青山。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taikang he moved again to Green Mountain on the Tu River.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang ten he moved to Green Mountain on the Tu River.

sentences.zh: 廆以大棘城即帝顓頊之墟也，元康四年乃移居之。

translations.literal: Hui held that Greater Jicheng stood on the ruins of Emperor Zhuanxu's capital; in the fourth year of Yuankang he relocated there.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt Greater Jicheng on Zhuanxu's legendary capital.

sentences.zh: 教以農桑，法制同于上國。

translations.literal: He taught farming and sericulture; laws mirrored the central states.
translations.idiomatic: He taught farming and Jin-style statutes.

sentences.zh: 永甯中，燕垂大水，廆開倉振給，幽方獲濟。

translations.literal: During Yongning terrible floods struck Yan; Hui opened granaries and relieved distress across Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning floods opened his granaries to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 天子聞而嘉之，褒賜命服。

translations.literal: The sovereign heard and praised him, awarding insignia robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with court robes.

sentences.zh: 太安初，宇文莫圭遣弟屈雲寇邊城，雲別帥大素延攻掠諸部，廆親擊敗之。

translations.literal: Early in Tai'an Yuwen Mogui sent brother Quyun to raid the frontier; Quyun's lieutenant Su Yan attacked neighboring tribes until Hui defeated him in person.
translations.idiomatic: Tai'an brought Yuwen raids he smashed personally.

sentences.zh: 素延怒，率眾十萬圍棘城，眾咸懼，人無距志。

translations.literal: Su Yan, furious, besieged Jicheng with a hundred thousand men; all feared and lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yan's hundred thousand terrified Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 廆曰：「素延雖犬羊蟻聚，然軍無法制，已在吾計中矣。

translations.literal: Hui said, "Though Yan herds dogs and ants together, his host lacks discipline—I already hold him in my plan.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed Su Yan's rabble as leaderless.

sentences.zh: 諸君但為力戰，無所憂也。

translations.literal: You gentlemen need only fight hard—have no fear."
translations.idiomatic: He promised victory if troops stood firm.

sentences.zh: 」乃躬貫甲胄，馳出擊之，素延大敗，追奔百里，俘斬萬餘人。

translations.literal: Donning armor himself, he sortied, routed Yan, chased a hundred li, and killed or captured over ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He personally crushed Su Yan and harvested ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，廆自稱鮮卑大單于。

translations.literal: Early in Yongjia Hui styled himself Great Shanyu of the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia opened with his claim to Great Shanyu.

sentences.zh: 遼東太守龐本以私憾殺東夷校尉李臻，附塞鮮卑素連、木津等托為臻報仇，實欲因而為亂，遂攻陷諸縣，殺掠士庶。

translations.literal: Liaodong governor Pang Ben slew Colonel of the Eastern Yi Li Zhen out of private spite; Sulian, Muqin, and other frontier Xianbei purported to avenge Zhen but meant rebellion—overrunning counties and slaughtering gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ben's murder of Li Zhen let Sulian and Muqin devastate Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 太守袁謙頻戰失利，校尉封釋懼而請和。

translations.literal: Governor Yuan Qian lost repeatedly; Colonel Feng Shi, frightened, sued for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qian stumbled while Feng Shi begged truce.

sentences.zh: 連歲寇掠，百姓失業，流亡歸附者日月相繼。

translations.literal: Years of raiding cost livelihoods; refugees flocked to Hui daily.
translations.idiomatic: Endless raiding sent refugees streaming to Murong lands.

sentences.zh: 廆子翰言於廆曰：「求諸侯莫如勤王，自古有為之君靡不杖此以成事業者也。

translations.literal: Hui's son Han said to him: "Nothing secures a lord like aiding the king—every founder has relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Han urged royalist war on the bandit chiefs.

sentences.zh: 今連、津跋扈，王師覆敗，蒼生屠膾，豈甚此乎！

translations.literal: Now Sulian and Muqin run rampant; imperial armies have fallen; the people are butchered—could it be worse?
translations.idiomatic: The slaughter exceeded anything earlier chaos had shown.

sentences.zh: 豎子外以龐本為名，內實幸而為寇。

translations.literal: Those rogues outwardly cite Pang Ben but inwardly rejoice in banditry.
translations.idiomatic: The warlords wore Pang Ben as their excuse.

sentences.zh: 封使君以誅本請和，而毒害滋深。

translations.literal: Commissioner Feng executed Ben to sue for peace yet poison deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shi's execution of Pang Ben bought no peace.

sentences.zh: 遼東傾沒，垂已二周，中原兵亂，州師屢敗，勤王杖義，今其時也。

translations.literal: Liaodong has collapsed two years running; the Central Plains war endlessly—now is the hour to aid the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Ruined Liaodong cried out for loyal arms.

sentences.zh: 單于宜明九伐之威，救倒懸之命，數連、津之罪，合義兵以誅之。

translations.literal: Our Shanyu should wield the nine punitive expeditions, rescue the hanging populace, denounce Sulian and Muqin, and rally righteous troops to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: He called for sanctioned campaigns against Sulian and Muqin.

sentences.zh: 上則興復遼邦，下則併吞二部，忠義彰於本朝，私利歸於我國，此則吾鴻漸之始也，終可以得志于諸侯。

translations.literal: Above we restore Liaodong; below we annex both tribes—loyalty shines at court while profit stays with us: this begins our rise among the lords."
translations.idiomatic: Victory would restore Liaodong, absorb both tribes, and broadcast Murong virtue.

sentences.zh: 」廆從之。

translations.literal: Hui agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 是日，率騎討連、津，大敗斬之，二部悉降，徙之棘城，立遼東郡而歸。

translations.literal: That day he struck Sulian and Muqin, crushed them, beheaded both leaders, accepted their tribes' surrender, moved them to Jicheng, founded Liaodong commandery, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He executed both chiefs, resettled tribes at Jicheng, and drew up Liaodong commandery.

sentences.zh: 懷帝蒙塵于平陽，王浚承制以廆為散騎常侍、冠軍將軍、前鋒大都督、大單于，廆不受。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai suffered at Pingyang, Wang Jun by interim authority offered Hui supernumerary attendant, Champion General, Forward Marshal, Great Shanyu—Hui declined.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's honors could not buy him.

sentences.zh: 建興中，湣帝遣使拜廆鎮軍將軍、昌黎、遼東二國公。

translations.literal: During Jianxing Emperor Min sent envoys to appoint Hui General Who Guards the Army and duke of Changli and Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min offered guard-general rank and twin ducal patents.

sentences.zh: 建武初，元帝承制拜廆假節、散騎常侍、都督遼左雜夷流人諸軍事、龍驤將軍、大單于、昌黎公，廆讓而不受。

translations.literal: Early in Jianwu Yuan-di by interim authority appointed Hui Bearer of Staff, Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Area Commander of Liaozuo miscellaneous barbarians and displaced persons, General of Dragon Soaring, Great Shanyu, Duke of Changli—Hui demurred.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang repeated appointments under Yuan-di; Hui still refused empty grandeur.

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍魯昌說廆曰：「今兩京傾沒，天子蒙塵，琅邪承制江東，實人命所系。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the Enemy Lu Chang urged Hui: "Both capitals have fallen and the Son of Heaven wanders; Langye rules Jiangdong by interim decree—the mandate of life and death rests there.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chang argued only imperial seals could awe rival tribes.

sentences.zh: 明公雄據海朔，跨總一方，而諸部猶怙眾稱兵，未遵道化者，蓋以官非王命，又自以為強。

translations.literal: My lord towers over the northern sea yet tribes still bear arms because your offices lack imperial seals and each thinks himself strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Murong prestige needed Jiankang's mandate.

sentences.zh: 今宜通使琅邪，勸承大統，然後敷宣帝命，以伐有罪，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: Send envoys to Langye urging enthronement, then proclaim imperial orders and punish the guilty—who would disobey?"
translations.idiomatic: Envoys pushing Yuan-di to enthrone himself could sanctify northern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 」廆善之，乃遣其長史王濟浮海勸進。

translations.literal: Hui approved and dispatched chief clerk Wang Ji by sea to urge Yuan-di to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Ji across the sea to urge enthronement.

sentences.zh: 及帝即尊位，遣謁者陶遼重申前命，授廆將軍、單于，廆固辭公封。

translations.literal: After the emperor assumed the throne, envoy Tao Liao renewed earlier commissions as general and Shanyu; Hui firmly declined ducal investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's envoy Tao Liao could not force ducal robes on him.

sentences.zh: 時二京傾覆，幽、冀淪陷，廆刑政修明，虛懷引納，流亡士庶多繈負歸之。

translations.literal: As both capitals collapsed and You-Ji fell, Hui governed clearly and welcomed exiles; scholars and commoners arrived carrying children on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Clear rule drew refugee elites carrying children on their backs.

sentences.zh: 廆乃立郡以統流人，冀州人為冀陽郡，豫州人為成周郡，青州人為營丘郡，并州人為唐國郡。

translations.literal: He founded commanderies for the displaced—Jiyang for Ji refugees, Chengzhou for Yu, Yingqiu for Qing, Tangguo for Bing.
translations.idiomatic: He grouped exiles into hometown prefectures.

sentences.zh: 於是推舉賢才，委以庶政，以河東裴嶷、代郡魯昌、北平陽耽為謀主，北海逢羨、廣平遊邃、北平西方虔、渤海封抽、西河宋奭、河東裴開為股肱，渤海封弈、平原宋該、安定皇甫岌、蘭陵繆愷以文章才俊任居樞要，會稽硃左車、太山胡毋翼、魯國孔纂以舊德清重引為賓友，平原劉贊儒學該通，引為東庠祭酒，其世子皝率國胄束修受業焉。

translations.literal: He promoted worthies to routine administration: Hedong Pei Yi, Dai commandery Lu Chang, Beiping Yang Dan as strategists; Beihai Feng Xian, Guangping You Sui, Beiping Fang Qian, Bohai Feng Chou, Xihe Song Shi, Hedong Pei Kai as arms and legs; Bohai Feng Yi, Pingyuan Song Gai, Anding Huangfu Qi, Lanling Miao Kai held literary portfolios; Kuaiji Zhu Zuoche, Taishan Humu Yi, Lu state Kong Zuan served as honored guests; Pingyuan Liu Zan's erudition made him Libationer of the eastern school where heir Huang studied.
translations.idiomatic: He staffed government with refugee scholars and set Liu Zan to teach heir Huang.

sentences.zh: 廆覽政之暇，親臨聽之，於是路有頌聲，禮讓興矣。

translations.literal: When governance permitted, Hui attended lectures himself; songs of praise spread and courtesy flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He audited the school himself until courtesy songs filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 時平州刺史、東夷校尉崔毖自以為南州士望，意存懷集，而流亡者莫有赴之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Pingzhou and Colonel Cui Bi deemed himself premier southern gentleman and wished to gather exiles, yet none came.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bi waited for refugees that Murong had already welcomed.

sentences.zh: 毖意廆拘留，乃陰結高句麗及宇文、段國等，謀滅廆以分其地。

translations.literal: Bi suspected Hui detained them and secretly allied Goguryeo, Yuwen, and Duan to destroy Murong and partition his land.
translations.idiomatic: Bi enlisted Goguryeo, Yuwen, and Duan against Murong territory.

sentences.zh: 太興初，三國伐廆，廆曰：「彼信崔毖虛說，邀一時之利，烏合而來耳。

translations.literal: Early in Taixing the three states attacked Hui; Hui said, "They trusted Cui Bi's lies for quick gain—this is a flock without cohesion.
translations.idiomatic: The triple alliance trusted Bi's fiction—ripe for divide-and-rule.

sentences.zh: 既無統一，莫相歸伏，吾今破之必矣。

translations.literal: They share no unified command or loyalty—I shall break them.
translations.idiomatic: Discord doomed their coalition.

sentences.zh: 然彼軍初合，其鋒甚銳，幸我速戰。

translations.literal: Their force is newly joined and keen—they hope we fight quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh allies wanted a quick pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 若逆擊之，落其計矣。

translations.literal: Meet them head-on and we fall into their trap.
translations.idiomatic: A hasty sally played into their trap.

sentences.zh: 靖以待之，必懷疑貳，迭相猜防。

translations.literal: Stay calm; mutual suspicion will divide them.
translations.idiomatic: Delay would breed mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 一則疑吾與毖譎而覆之，二則自疑三國之中與吾有韓魏之謀者，待其人情沮惑，然後取之必矣。

translations.literal: First they will suspect us colluding with Bi against them; second each ally will fear Han-Wei-style betrayal among themselves—when morale collapses we strike and win."
translations.idiomatic: Each ally would fear Jin-style double-dealing until morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 」於是三國攻棘城，廆閉門不戰，遣使送牛酒以犒宇文，大言於眾曰：「崔毖昨有使至。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three states assaulted Jicheng; Hui barred the gates and refused battle, sending cattle and wine to refresh the Yuwen while proclaiming to the host, "Cui Bi had envoys here yesterday."
translations.idiomatic: He locked Jicheng and staged a fake tryst with Bi's envoys before the Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 」於是二國果疑宇文同於廆也，引兵而歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon the two states suspected Yuwen colluded with Hui and withdrew their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Two allies suspected Yuwen treachery and marched home.

sentences.zh: 宇文悉獨官曰：「二國雖歸，吾當獨兼其國，何用人為！

translations.literal: Yuwen Siduguan said, "Though both allies retreat, I alone shall annex their lands—why need others!"
translations.idiomatic: Siduguan vowed to seize their lands alone.

sentences.zh: 」盡眾逼城，連營三十里。

translations.literal: He brought every man against the city, linking camps for thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: He stacked thirty li of camps around Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 廆簡銳士配皝，推鋒於前；

translations.literal: Hui picked elite troops for Huang and drove the vanguard forward;
translations.idiomatic: He gave Huang crack troops for the van.

sentences.zh: 翰領精騎為奇兵，從旁出，直沖其營；

translations.literal: Han led crack cavalry as a surprise corps, swung out from the flank, and pierced straight into their camp;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Han struck the flank with elite horse.

sentences.zh: 廆方陣而進。

translations.literal: Hui advanced in square formation.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rolled forward in formation.

sentences.zh: 悉獨官自恃其眾，不設備，見廆軍之至，方率兵距之。

translations.literal: Siduguan trusted his numbers, posted no precautions; only when Murong troops arrived did he hurry to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Siduguan's overconfidence left camps wide open.

sentences.zh: 前鋒始交，翰已入其營，縱火焚之，其眾皆震擾，不知所為，遂大敗，悉獨官僅以身免，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: As the van joined battle Han had already entered the camp, set fires, and threw them into panic—they routed utterly; Siduguan barely escaped alive and his entire force was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Han's raid fired Yuwen tents and shattered their host.

sentences.zh: 於是營候獲皇帝玉璽三紐，遣長史裴嶷送於建鄴。

translations.literal: Camp guards then seized three cords of the imperial jade seal; chief clerk Pei Yi sent them to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Captives yielded imperial seal cords sent south to Jiankye.

sentences.zh: 崔毖懼廆之仇己也，使兄子燾偽賀廆。

translations.literal: Fearing Hui's vengeance Cui Bi sent nephew Tao with false congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Bi feigned congratulations through nephew Tao.

sentences.zh: 會三國使亦至請和，曰：「非我本意也，崔平州教我耳。

translations.literal: When envoys from all three states also arrived suing for peace they said, "This was never our intent—Inspector Cui Pingzhou urged us."
translations.idiomatic: The allied envoys blamed Pingzhou inspector Cui Bi.

sentences.zh: 」廆將燾示以攻圍之處，臨之以兵，曰：「汝叔父教三國滅我，何以詐來賀我乎？

translations.literal: Hui showed Tao the siege lines and ringed him with troops: "Your uncle taught three states to destroy me—why pretend congratulations?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui trapped Tao and exposed Bi's plot.

sentences.zh: 」廆懼，首服。

translations.literal: Bi in terror submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Bi groveled in terror.

sentences.zh: 廆乃遣燾歸說毖曰：「降者上策，走者下策也。

translations.literal: Hui sent Tao back to persuade Bi: "Surrender is the best plan; flight the worst."
translations.idiomatic: Hui offered surrender or flight.

sentences.zh: 」以兵隨之。

translations.literal: Troops followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Troops pressed Bi toward decision.

sentences.zh: 毖與數十騎棄家室奔於高句麗，廆悉降其眾，徙燾及高瞻等於棘城，待以賓禮。

translations.literal: Bi fled with several dozen riders toward Goguryeo abandoning family; Hui accepted his followers, moved Tao and Gao Zhan and others to Jicheng, and treated them as guests.
translations.idiomatic: Bi fled to Goguryeo while Murong settled his people at Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，高句麗寇遼東，廆遣眾擊敗之。

translations.literal: Next year Goguryeo raided Liaodong; Hui sent troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong troops beat back Goguryeo's next Liaodong raid.

sentences.zh: 裴嶷至自建鄴，帝遣使者拜廆監平州諸軍事、安北將軍、平州刺史，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When Pei Yi returned from Jianye the emperor dispatched envoys appointing Hui Inspector of Pingzhou military affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Pingzhou, with two thousand added households.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi's return brought Pingzhou inspector titles and added fiefs.

sentences.zh: 尋加使持節、都督幽州東夷諸軍事、車騎將軍、平州牧，進封遼東郡公，邑一萬戶，常侍、單于並如故；

translations.literal: Soon he added Bearer of Staff, Area Commander of Youzhou and Eastern Yi military affairs, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Shepherd of Pingzhou, advanced to Duke of Liaodong commandery with ten thousand households; palace attendant and Shanyu titles unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He gained staff authority, chariot-and-cavalry command, Liaodong duke with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 丹書鐵券，承制海東，命備官司，置平州守宰。

translations.literal: He received vermilion writ and iron tally and imperial mandate east of the sea to establish full bureaucracy with Pingzhou magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion writ and iron tally let him staff Pingzhou east of the sea.

sentences.zh: 段末波初統其國，而不修備，廆遣皝襲之，入令支，收其名馬寶物而還。

translations.literal: When Duan Mobo first ruled his state without readiness Hui sent Huang to raid him, entered Lingzhi, seized famed horses and treasures, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He raided unprepared Duan Mobo at Lingzhi for horses and loot.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣使通和，廆距之。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent envoys seeking friendship; Hui refused.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuffed Shi Le's overtures.

sentences.zh: 送其使於建鄴。

translations.literal: He forwarded Le's envoys to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: He shipped Later Zhao envoys south to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 勒怒，遣宇文乞得龜擊廆，廆遣皝距之。

translations.literal: Enraged, Le sent the Yuwen chieftain Qidegui to attack Hui; Hui sent Murong Huang to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le answered Murong's snub by ordering Yuwen Qidegui north; Huang blocked him.

sentences.zh: 以裴嶷為右部都督，率索頭為右翼，命其少子仁自平郭趣柏林為左翼，攻乞得龜，克之，悉虜其眾。

translations.literal: With Pei Yi as commander of the right wing, he led Suotou cavalry on the right; he ordered his youngest son Ren from Pinggu toward Bailin on the left; they attacked Qidegui, defeated him, and captured his entire host.
translations.idiomatic: Huang split wings—Pei Yi and Suotou on the right, Ren circling from Pinggu—crushing Qidegui.

sentences.zh: 乘勝拔其國城，收其資用億計，徙其人數萬戶以歸。

translations.literal: Following victory they stormed his capital, seized supplies reckoned in hundreds of millions, and moved tens of thousands of households home.
translations.idiomatic: They looted the Yuwen capital and resettled tens of thousands southward.

sentences.zh: 成帝即位，加廆侍中，位特進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng succeeded to the throne Hui was additionally appointed palace attendant with specially advanced rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi added him palace attendant with eminent precedence.

sentences.zh: 咸和五年，又加開府儀同三司，固辭不受。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianhe he was further granted independent headquarters with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He refused Three-Duke parity again in Xianhe five.

sentences.zh: 廆嘗從容言曰：「獄者，人命之所懸也，不可以不慎。

translations.literal: Hui once remarked at ease: "Prisons suspend men's lives—there must be no carelessness."
translations.idiomatic: He warned that justice holds lives in the balance.

sentences.zh: 賢人君子，國家之基也，不可以不敬。

translations.literal: The worthy and the gentleman are the state's foundation—they cannot go unhonored.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted rulers must honor worthy men.

sentences.zh: 稼穡者，國之本也，不可以不急。

translations.literal: Agriculture is the state's root—it cannot be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked farming as the dynastic bedrock.

sentences.zh: 酒色便佞，亂德之甚也，不可以不戒。

translations.literal: Wine, women, and flatterers ruin virtue worst—they demand vigilance.
translations.idiomatic: He condemned debauchery that unmakes rule.

sentences.zh: 」乃著《家令》數千言以申其旨。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed the \Household Instructions\" in several thousand words to spell out these aims."
translations.idiomatic: He codified family maxims expounding those themes.

sentences.zh: 遣使與太尉陶侃箋曰：

translations.literal: He sent an envoy with a letter to Grand Commandant Tao Kan:
translations.idiomatic: His letter to Tao Kan began:

sentences.zh: 明公使君轂下：振德曜威，撫甯方夏，勞心文武，士馬無恙，欽高仰止，注情彌久。

translations.literal: Noble lord under your carriage wheels: you spread virtue and awe, pacifying the realm; civil and military labor leaves your horses unharmed—we admire you ever more and long have fixed our hearts on you.
translations.idiomatic: He flattered Tao Kan's prestige on the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 王途險遠，隔以燕越，每瞻江湄，延首遐外。

translations.literal: The royal road is rugged and far, Yan and Yue divide us; each time we gaze toward the river's edge we stretch our necks beyond the horizon.
translations.idiomatic: Geography severed Murong from court.

sentences.zh: 天降艱難，禍害屢臻，舊都不守，奄為虜庭，使皇輿遷幸，假勢吳、楚。

translations.literal: Heaven has sent hardship—calamities pile up; the old capital could not be held and became barbarian halls; the imperial carriage moved by grace into Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned Luoyang's fall and the court's exile south.

sentences.zh: 大晉啟基、祚流萬節，天命未改，玄象著明，是以義烈之士深懷憤踴。

translations.literal: Great Jin began its mandate and fortune flowed ten thousand generations—Heaven's mandate is unchanged and stellar signs are bright; thus righteous warriors harbor fierce resolve.
translations.idiomatic: He asserted Jin's cosmic legitimacy survived.

sentences.zh: 猥以功薄，受國殊寵，上不能掃除群羯，下不能身赴國難，仍縱賊臣，屢逼京輦。

translations.literal: I am ashamed that my merit is slight yet I receive extraordinary grace from the state—above I cannot wipe out the Jie hordes, below I cannot rush to national disaster; traitors still besiege the throne again and again.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed Murong power insufficient alone while rebels threatened Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 王敦唱禍于前，蘇峻肆毒於後，凶暴過於董卓，惡逆甚於傕、汜，普天率土，誰不同忿！

translations.literal: Wang Dun raised calamity before; Su Jun poisoned the realm after—viciousness surpassed Dong Zhuo; treason exceeded Li Jue and Guo Si—who under heaven does not share the rage!
translations.idiomatic: He catalogued Jin's domestic rebels beside Han villains.

sentences.zh: 深怪文武之士，過荷朝榮，不能滅中原之寇，刷天下之恥。

translations.literal: I deeply wonder why civil and military gentlemen, burdened with court glory, cannot destroy central-plain bandits and wash away the empire's shame.
translations.idiomatic: He reproached southern ministers for inertia against Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 君侯植根江陽，發曜荊、衡，杖葉公之權，有包胥之志，而令白公、伍員殆得極其暴，竊為丘明恥之。

translations.literal: You, lord, are rooted along the Yangzi, shine between Jing and Heng, wield Lord Ye's authority and harbor Shen Baoxu's resolve—yet Bai Gong and Wu Yuan ran riot—history would shame Qiu Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Tao Kan to emulate Chu loyalists against barbarians.

sentences.zh: 區區楚國子重之徒，猶恥君弱、群臣不及先大夫，厲己戒眾，以服陳、鄭；

translations.literal: Even Chu ministers like Zichong were ashamed when their lord was weak and officers fell short of earlier leaders—they disciplined themselves to humble Chen and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Spring and Autumn shame-forged virtue.

sentences.zh: 越之種蠡尚能弼佐句踐，取威黃池；

translations.literal: Yue's Zhongli and Fan Li still aided Goujian to glory at Huangchi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu-Yue precedent proved peripheral grit could win.

sentences.zh: 況今吳土英賢比肩，而不輔翼聖主，陵江北伐。

translations.literal: How much more today Wu soil teams with heroes—yet none assists the sage sovereign to sweep north.
translations.idiomatic: He contrasted Wu talent with southern lethargy.

sentences.zh: 以義聲之直，討逆暴之羯，檄命舊邦之士，招懷存本之人，豈不若因風振落，頓阪走輪哉！

translations.literal: With righteous prestige you could punish cruel Jie bandits, issue orders to old heartlands, summon homesick people—is it not like shaking leaves in wind or wheels racing downhill!
translations.idiomatic: Northern expedition should sweep Shi Le easily.

sentences.zh: 且孫氏之初，以長沙之眾摧破董卓，志匡漢室。

translations.literal: Moreover Sun's house began by crushing Dong Zhuo with Changsha's host and aiming to restore Han.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian's loyalty anchored Wu rise.

sentences.zh: 雖中遇寇害，雅志不遂，原其心誠，乃忽身命。

translations.literal: Though mid-course setbacks thwarted noble aims, judging original intent they threw away life for loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun lineage sacrifice deserved respect.

sentences.zh: 及權據揚、越，外杖周、張，內馮顧、陸，距魏亦壁，克取襄陽。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan held Yang and Yue, Zhou Yu and Zhang Zhao outside, Gu Yong and Lu Xun inside, he checked Wei at the river and seized Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's teamwork humbled northern power.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，世主相襲，咸能侵逼徐、豫，令魏朝旰食。

translations.literal: Thereafter each ruler inherited ambition and pressed Xu and Yu so Wei ate meals late with worry.
translations.idiomatic: Successive Wu kings threatened central plains.

sentences.zh: 不知今之江表為賢俊匿智，藏其勇略邪？

translations.literal: Do today's Jiangnan talents hide wisdom and bury valor?
translations.idiomatic: He challenged southern elites to show courage.

sentences.zh: 將呂蒙、淩統高蹤曠世哉？

translations.literal: Are they inferior to Lü Meng and Ling Tong?
translations.idiomatic: He invoked Wu's famed commanders.

sentences.zh: 況今凶羯虐暴，中州人士逼迫勢促，其顛沛之危，甚於累卵。

translations.literal: Moreover vicious Jie tyranny squeezes central-plain families worse than stacked eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Chinese suffered imminent ruin under Shi.

sentences.zh: 假號之強，眾心所去，敵有釁矣，易可震盪。

translations.literal: The false emperor's might lacks popular support; enemies show cracks—easy to shake apart.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's regime was brittle.

sentences.zh: 王郎、袁術雖自詐偽，皆基淺根微，禍不旋踵，此皆君侯之所聞見者矣。

translations.literal: Wang Lang and Yuan Shu were frauds yet shallow-rooted—their doom swift; all this you yourself have witnessed.
translations.idiomatic: Pseudo-emperors fell quickly before true mandate.

sentences.zh: 王司徒清虛寡欲，善於全己，昔曹參亦綜此道，著畫一之稱也。

translations.literal: Director Wang Dao is clear-minded with few desires, skilled at preserving himself—like Han's Cao Shen who earned praise for consistent rule.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Wang Dao's quiet survival craft.

sentences.zh: 庾公居元舅之尊，處申伯之任，超然高蹈，明智之權。

translations.literal: Yu Liang enjoys honoured maternal standing like Shen Bo yet stays aloof—wise discretion.
translations.idiomatic: He noted Yu Liang's cautious stance.

sentences.zh: 廆於寇難之際，受大晉累世之恩，自恨絕域，無益聖朝，徒系心萬里，望風懷憤。

translations.literal: Hui amid invasion bears generations of Great Jin grace yet regrets remote borders cannot aid the holy court—only ties heart to capital ten thousand li away, nursing rage on the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Murong loyalty endured despite distance.

sentences.zh: 今海內之望，足為楚、漢輕重者，惟在君侯。

translations.literal: Among powers under heaven only you, lord, weigh like Chu or Han contenders.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan alone could tip balance.

sentences.zh: 若戮力盡心，悉五州之眾，據兗、豫之郊，使向義之士倒戈釋甲，則羯寇必滅，國恥必除。

translations.literal: If you marshal five provinces, seize Yan-Yu borders, make righteous men lay down arms and armor, Jie bandits perish and national shame washes away.
translations.idiomatic: Joint northward strike could restore Jin.

sentences.zh: 廆在一方，敢不竭命。

translations.literal: Hui holds one corner yet dares exhaust every fiber.
translations.idiomatic: Murong pledged full support from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 孤軍輕進，不足使勒畏首畏尾，則懷舊之士欲為內應，無由自發故也。

translations.literal: A lone thrust north cannot make Le tremble head and tail unless sympathizers inside rise—without coordination they cannot act.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinated fronts needed secret Jin allies.

sentences.zh: 故遠陳寫，言不宣盡。

translations.literal: Thus I write at length though words cannot exhaust intent.
translations.idiomatic: Letter ran long by necessity.

sentences.zh: 廆使者遭風沒海。

translations.literal: Hui's envoy perished when winds wrecked the ship at sea.
translations.idiomatic: The first embassy drowned crossing the sea.

sentences.zh: 其後廆更寫前箋，並齎其東夷校尉封抽、行遼東相韓矯等三十餘人疏上侃府曰：

translations.literal: Later Hui rewrote the earlier letter and together with Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, acting Liaodong minister Han Jiao, and thirty others memorialized Tao Kan's headquarters:
translations.idiomatic: Murong coordinated a joint petition southward.

sentences.zh: 自古有國有家，鮮不極盛而衰。

translations.literal: Since antiquity states and houses rarely avoid rising to utmost splendor then declining.
translations.idiomatic: Opening lament on dynastic cycles.

sentences.zh: 自大晉龍興，克平㟭、會，神武之略，邁蹤前史。

translations.literal: When Great Jin arose like a dragon it pacified Ba-Shu and Kuaiji—martial spirit surpassed former histories.
translations.idiomatic: Jin founding triumphs outshone antiquity.

sentences.zh: 惠皇之末，後黨構難，禍結京畿，釁成公族，遂使羯寇乘虛，傾覆諸夏，舊都淪滅，山陵毀掘，人神悲悼，幽明發憤。

translations.literal: Late under Emperor Hui empress faction strife tangled the capital and princes fought until Jie bandits exploited void and overturned the Central Plains—the old capital sank and imperial tombs were dug—men and spirits mourned and gods blazed anger.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's reign disasters enabled Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 昔獫狁之強，匈奴之盛，未有如今日羯寇之暴，跨躡華裔，盜稱尊號者也。

translations.literal: Never did mighty Xianyun nor powerful Xiongnu match today's Jie scourge straddling Chinese and barbarian and stealing imperial titles.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le exceeded ancient northern foes.

sentences.zh: 天祚有晉，挺授英傑。

translations.literal: Heaven blesses Jin and raises heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Divine aid sustained Jin survivors.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍慕容廆自弱冠蒞國，忠於王室，明允恭肅，志在立勳。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Murong Hui since youth held his country loyal to the royal house—trustworthy, reverent, resolved on merit.
translations.idiomatic: Petition praised Murong youth and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 屬海內分崩，皇輿遷幸，元皇中興，初唱大業，肅祖繼統，蕩平江外。

translations.literal: As the realm shattered and the imperial carriage shifted, Yuan-di revived enterprise midstream and Su zu continued, sweeping peace beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: Southern courts sustained mandate.

sentences.zh: 廆雖限以山海，隔以羯寇，翹首引領，系心京師，常假寤寐，欲憂國忘身。

translations.literal: Though mountains and seas fence Hui from Jie bandits he cranes his neck toward capital, hearts tied to Luoyang, sleepless with longing to forget self for state.
translations.idiomatic: Murong fixation on restoration despite barriers.

sentences.zh: 貢篚相尋，連舟載路，戎不稅駕，動成義舉。

translations.literal: Tribute baskets followed one another and barges jammed the route—without pausing harness he acted righteously.
translations.idiomatic: Steady tribute demonstrated virtue.

sentences.zh: 今羯寇滔天，怙其丑類，樹基趙、魏，跨略燕、齊。

translations.literal: Now Jie flood heaven; relying on rabble they rooted Zhao-Wei and span Yan-Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's realm sprawled north.

sentences.zh: 廆雖率義眾，誅討大逆，然管仲相齊，猶曰寵不足以禦下，況廆輔翼王室，有匡霸之功，而位卑爵輕，九命未加，非所以寵異籓翰，敦獎殊勳者也。

translations.literal: Though Hui leads righteous hosts punishing great rebellion, even Guan Zhong aiding Qi said petty favors cannot command subordinates—how much less Hui aiding royal house with hegemonic merit yet low rank and light fiefs without nine honors—not how to exalt a frontier pillar or reward extraordinary deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Petition argued Murong deserved kingly rank to command allies.

sentences.zh: 方今詔命隔絕，王路險遠，貢使往來，動彌年載。

translations.literal: Today edicts are cut off and royal roads deadly—envoys take years round-trip.
translations.idiomatic: Communication lag hindered investiture.

sentences.zh: 今燕之舊壤，北周沙漠，東盡樂浪，西暨代山，南極冀方，而悉為虜庭，非復國家之域。

translations.literal: Former Yan lands north ring desert, east reach Ledong, west touch Dai peaks, south border Ji lands—now all barbarian halls, no longer Jin terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Geographic loss demanded counter-title.

sentences.zh: 將佐等以為宜遠遵周室，近准漢初，進封廆為燕王，行大將軍事，上以總統諸部，下以割損賊境。

translations.literal: Staff officers deem we should follow Zhou models and Han precedent—advance Hui as King of Yan with acting grand-general powers to unite tribes above and shear enemy lands below.
translations.idiomatic: Petition requested Murong kinghood like Han vassals.

sentences.zh: 使冀州之人望風向化。

translations.literal: Let Ji provincials face virtue and convert.
translations.idiomatic: Royal patent would sway northerners.

sentences.zh: 廆得祗承詔命，率合諸國，奉辭夷逆，以成桓文之功，苟利社稷，專之可也。

translations.literal: Hui receiving decree could harmonize states, marshal rhetoric against barbarians, finish Huan-Wen-style achievement—if altars profit, specialized mandate fits.
translations.idiomatic: Kingship empowered lawful campaigns.

sentences.zh: 而廆固執謙光，守節彌高，每詔所加，讓動積年，非將佐等所能敦逼。

translations.literal: Yet Hui modestly declines, integrity ever higher—each edict he refuses for years; staff cannot coerce him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong humility delayed acceptance.

sentences.zh: 今區區所陳，不欲苟相崇重，而愚情至心，實為國計。

translations.literal: Our petty plea seeks not empty flattery but earnest policy for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Petitioners stressed practical need.

sentences.zh: 侃報抽等書，其略曰：「車騎將軍憂國忘身，貢篚載路，羯賊求和，執使送之，西討段國，北伐塞外，遠綏索頭，荒服以獻。

translations.literal: Kan replied to Feng Chou's letter in gist: \General of Chariots and Cavalry forgets self for the state—tribute baskets crowd the road; Jie bandits sued peace yet he handed envoys to court; he struck west at Duan lands, campaigned north beyond the passes, soothed Suotou tribes—distant desert peoples submitted tribute.\""
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan praised Murong's loyalty and frontier victories.

sentences.zh: 惟北部未賓，屢遣征伐。

translations.literal: Only the northern tribes remained unsubdued despite repeated campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Northern raids still troubled Murong.

sentences.zh: 又知東方官號，高下齊班，進無統攝之權，退無等差之降，欲進車騎為燕王，一二具之。

translations.literal: He also explained eastern titles lacked unified hierarchy—none commanded others—so advancing the general as King of Yan needed clarification.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern offices needed royal coordination before king-making.

sentences.zh: 夫功成進爵，古之成制也。

translations.literal: Merit earns advancement—ancient norm.
translations.idiomatic: Tao cited precedent for promotion.

sentences.zh: 車騎雖未能為官摧勒，然忠義竭誠。

translations.literal: Though the general cannot yet crush Le in office, his loyalty is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He acknowledged logistical limits yet praised devotion.

sentences.zh: 今騰箋上聽，可不遲速，當任天臺也。

translations.literal: Now his memorial reaches us—delay must not tarry; Heaven's terrace decides.
translations.idiomatic: Tao would forward petition to court.

sentences.zh: 」朝議未定。

translations.literal: The court debated without settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang stalled on investiture.

sentences.zh: 八年，廆卒，乃止。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Hui died—thereupon debate ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's death in Xianhe eight ended king talks.

sentences.zh: 時年六十五，在位四十九年。

translations.literal: He was sixty-five sui and had held authority forty-nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Murong ruled forty-nine years at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者策贈大將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys posthumously awarding Grand General and independent headquarters equal Three Dukes—posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Court gave posthumous honors Xiang.

sentences.zh: 及俊僭號，偽諡武宣皇帝。

translations.literal: When Murong Jun took imperial pretense he canonized him Martial-Proclaimer Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Later Former Yan canonized Wu-Xuan.

sentences.zh: 裴嶷，字文冀，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Yi, courtesy name Wenji, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi bio opens—style Wenji, Hedong Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 父昶，司隸校尉。

translations.literal: His father Chang had been Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Father Pei Chang held metropolitan colonel rank.

sentences.zh: 嶷清方有幹略，累遷至中書侍郎，轉給事黃門郎、滎陽太守。

translations.literal: Yi was upright and capable, rising to gentleman of the palace secretariat, then Huangmen gent., governor of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pei climbed central posts before chaos.

sentences.zh: 屬天下亂，嶷兄武先為玄菟太守，嶷遂求為昌黎太守。

translations.literal: As the realm collapsed his elder brother Wu first governed Xuandu; Yi sought appointment as Changli governor.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued Changli post near Murong.

sentences.zh: 至郡，久之，武卒，嶷被征，乃將武子開送喪俱南。

translations.literal: Long after reaching the commandery Wu died; Yi was recalled—escorting Wu's son Kai south for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Death recalled him with nephew Kai.

sentences.zh: 既達遼西，道路梗塞，乃與開投廆。

translations.literal: Reaching Liaoxi the roads were blocked so he and Kai joined Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoxi obstruction drove him to Murong.

sentences.zh: 時諸流寓之士見廆草創，並懷去就。

translations.literal: Then refugee gentlemen saw Murong still founding his state and hesitated whether to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Early refugees wavered over Murong's regime.

sentences.zh: 嶷首定名分，為群士啟行。

translations.literal: Yi first fixed hierarchy of ranks and opened the way for scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi imposed order on refugee protocols.

sentences.zh: 廆甚悅，以嶷為長史，委以軍國之謀。

translations.literal: Hui rejoiced, appointed Yi chief clerk, entrusting civil and military counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Murong made him chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 及悉獨官寇逼城下，外內騷動，廆問策於嶷，嶷曰：「悉獨官雖擁大眾，軍無號令，眾無部陣，若簡精兵，乘其無備，則成擒耳。

translations.literal: When Siduguan pressed the city walls and turmoil seized inside and outside Hui asked Yi for counsel Yi said: \Siduguan masses a crowd yet lacks orders or formations—pick elite troops and strike unprepared—he can be captured.\""
translations.idiomatic: Pei planned strike on disorderly Yuwen host.

sentences.zh: 」廆從之，遂陷寇營。

translations.literal: Hui followed him and overran the barbarian camp.
translations.idiomatic: The raid succeeded on Pei's advice.

sentences.zh: 廆威德於此甚振，將遣使獻捷於建鄴，妙簡行人，令嶷將命。

translations.literal: Hui's prestige surged; preparing envoys to present victory at Jiankye he chose Yi to bear the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi chosen for Jiankang embassy.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷以廆僻在荒遠，猶以邊裔之豪處之。

translations.literal: At first court treated Murong as distant frontier chief.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang underestimated Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 嶷既使至，盛言廆威略，又知四海英賢並為其用，舉朝改觀焉。

translations.literal: Once Yi arrived he stressed Murong's might and showed how heroes empire-wide served him—the whole court revised its view.
translations.idiomatic: His briefing rewrote metropolitan opinion.

sentences.zh: 嶷將還，帝試留嶷以觀之，嶷辭曰：「臣世荷朝恩，濯纓華省，因事遠寄，投跡荒遐。

translations.literal: As Yi prepared to return the emperor tested keeping Yi to observe him; Yi declined: \My house owes dynastic grace—I washed cap tints in the capital before exile drove me to wilderness.\""
translations.idiomatic: Pei declined detention citing Jin loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今遭開泰，得睹朝廷，復賜恩詔，即留京輦，於臣之私，誠為厚幸。

translations.literal: Now renewal lets me see court again and gracious edict would detain me—personally blessed.
translations.idiomatic: He honored imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 顧以皇居播遷，山陵幽辱，慕容龍驤將軍越在遐表，乃心王室，慷慨之誠，義感天地，方掃平中壤，奉迎皇輿，故遣使臣，萬里表誠。

translations.literal: But imperial residence wanders and tombs suffer shame while Murong Dragon-Soaring general waits beyond the frontier—heart tied to royal house, righteous passion touching Heaven and Earth—intent to sweep central plains and escort the imperial carriage—therefore sent envoys declaring sincerity ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: He justified returning to Murong's restoration cause.

sentences.zh: 今若留臣，必謂國家遺其僻陋，孤其丹心，使懷義懈怠。

translations.literal: If you detain me folk will say court despises frontier worthies and chills loyal hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Detention would wound Murong morale.

sentences.zh: 是以微臣區區忘身為國，貪還反命耳。

translations.literal: Thus your petty servant forgets body for state—greedy only to report back.
translations.idiomatic: Pei insisted on returning envoy duty.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: \You speak rightly.\""
translations.idiomatic: Court conceded.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣嶷還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Yi back.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi returned north.

sentences.zh: 廆後謂群僚曰：「裴長史名重中朝，而降屈於此，豈非天以授孤也。

translations.literal: Hui later told officials: \Chief Clerk Pei bears renowned weight in central court yet bends to us—is Heaven not gifting him to me?\""
translations.idiomatic: Murong hailed Pei as heaven-sent.

sentences.zh: 」出為遼東相，轉樂浪太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Liaodong minister then transferred governor of Langle.
translations.idiomatic: Pei governed Liaodong then Langle.

sentences.zh: 高瞻，字子前，渤海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Gao Zhan, courtesy name Ziqian, was a man of Xiu in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan bio—style Ziqian, Bohai Xiu.

sentences.zh: 少而英爽有俊才，身長八尺二寸。

translations.literal: In youth he was bright and talented, eight chi two cun tall.
translations.idiomatic: Gao stood eight chi two cun.

sentences.zh: 光熙中，調補尚書郎。

translations.literal: In the Guangxi era he was transferred to gentleman of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi posting brought him to ministry.

sentences.zh: 屬永嘉之亂，還鄉里，乃與父老議曰：「今皇綱不振，兵革雲擾，此郡沃壤，憑固河海，若兵荒歲儉，必為寇庭，非謂圖安之所。

translations.literal: When Yongjia turmoil struck he returned home and debated elders: \Imperial net slackens and armies swarm—this fertile coast behind rivers and sea—if famine hits war it becomes bandit ground—not where we seek safety.\""
translations.idiomatic: He urged abandoning Bohai for safer refuge.

sentences.zh: 王彭祖先在幽、薊，據燕、代之資，兵強國富，可以托也。

translations.literal: Wang Pengzu formerly held You-Ji—drawing on Yan-Dai resources his soldiers were strong and state rich—a worthy refuge.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to Wang Jun's Yan stronghold.

sentences.zh: 諸君以為何如？

translations.literal: What do gentlemen think?
translations.idiomatic: He polled elders.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸善之。

translations.literal: The gathered elders all declared it sound.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly endorsed his plan.

sentences.zh: 乃與叔父隱率數千家北徙幽州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and his uncle Yin led several thousand households north into Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He and Uncle Yin marched thousands north toward Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而以王浚政令無恆，乃依崔毖，隨毖如遼東。

translations.literal: Later, finding Wang Jun's orders capricious, they attached themselves to Cui Bi and followed him into Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's erratic rule drove them under Cui Bi toward Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 毖之與三國謀伐廆也，瞻固諫以為不可，毖不從。

translations.literal: When Bi plotted with three states to strike Murong Hui, Zhan remonstrated firmly that it must not be done—Bi refused to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan warned against Cui Bi's triple alliance; Bi ignored him.

sentences.zh: 及毖奔敗，瞻隨眾降於廆。

translations.literal: When Bi fled in defeat Zhan joined the crowd surrendering to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: After Bi's rout Zhan submitted with the refugees.

sentences.zh: 廆署為將軍，瞻稱疾不起。

translations.literal: Hui appointed him general but Zhan pleaded illness and would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Murong named him general; Zhan feigned sickness.

sentences.zh: 廆敬其姿器，數臨候之，撫其心曰：「君之疾在此，不在餘也。

translations.literal: Hui respected his stature and repeatedly visited, pressing a hand to his chest: "Your ailment lies here, nowhere else."
translations.idiomatic: Murong pressed him personally, insisting shame not sickness stalled him.

sentences.zh: 今天子播越，四海分崩，蒼生紛擾，莫知所系，孤思與諸君匡復帝室，翦鯨豕於二京，迎天子于吳、會，廓清八表，侔勳古烈，此孤之心也，孤之願也。

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven wanders, the realm splinters, the people drift anchorless—I desire with you gentlemen to restore the imperial house, cut whale-like foes from both capitals, welcome the emperor at Wu and Kuaiji, cleanse the eight quarters, rival ancient heroes—that is my heart and wish.
translations.idiomatic: Murong proclaimed plans to sweep bandits from Luoyang and Chang'an and escort Jin home.

sentences.zh: 君中州大族，冠冕之餘，宜痛心疾首，枕戈待旦，柰何以華夷之異，有懷介然。

translations.literal: You stem from great houses of the Central Plain, remnants of titled courts—you should ache with rage and sleep beside spears awaiting dawn—how can Chinese versus barbarian divide your loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: He urged Zhan to shed ethnic prejudice for restoration.

sentences.zh: 且大禹出於西羌，文王生於東夷，但問志略何如耳，豈以殊俗不可降心乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Yu the Great rose from western Qiang; King Wen was born among eastern Yi—only ambition matters—must foreign customs block sincere hearts!
translations.idiomatic: He cited sage kings born beyond Huaxia.

sentences.zh: 」瞻仍辭疾篤，廆深不平之。

translations.literal: Zhan still pleaded grave illness; Hui nursed deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan stayed "ill"; Murong grew bitter.

sentences.zh: 瞻又與宋該有隙，該陰勸廆除之。

translations.literal: Zhan also quarreled with Song Gai; Gai secretly urged Hui to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Gai baited Murong to execute Zhan.

sentences.zh: 瞻聞其言，彌不自安，遂以憂死。

translations.literal: When Zhan heard he grew ever more fearful and died of anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the plot terrified Zhan to death.
